questions.question: After loading a GLB with GLTFLoader, the model appears at a random position and is either tiny or enormous. What is the standard fix?
options: Pass a scale parameter directly to GLTFLoader
Compute a Box3 bounding box, then reposition and scale the model to fit a known unit size
Use OrbitControls to let the user manually find the model
Switch to OBJLoader which handles sizing automatically
questions.explanation: GLTFLoader does not normalize scale or origin. You must compute a Box3 bounding box with setFromObject(), extract the center and max dimension, then translate and scale the gltf.scene to fit your desired unit size.

questions.question: Why should you call renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2)) instead of just renderer.setPixelRatio(window.devicePixelRatio)?
options: Three.js throws an error if pixel ratio exceeds 2
Devices with DPR above 2 provide no visible quality gain but significantly increase GPU workload
Pixel ratios above 2 cause texture loading failures
The canvas element does not support DPR values higher than 2
questions.explanation: Rendering at 3x or 4x pixel ratio on high-DPI devices offers no meaningful visual improvement to the viewer but can triple the number of pixels the GPU must process, harming performance and battery life.

questions.question: You show a <canvas> element as the Three.js rendering target inside a hero section. The canvas looks blurry when first displayed, before the GLB loads. What should you add?
options: A CSS spinner overlay that is hidden in the GLTFLoader onLoad callback
A second canvas showing a placeholder shape
A setTimeout to delay scene initialization
The alpha: false option on WebGLRenderer
questions.explanation: Show a loading spinner (or skeleton) positioned absolutely over the canvas, then hide it inside the GLTFLoader onLoad callback. This prevents a confusing blank or partially-rendered canvas state during the network fetch.

questions.question: Which Three.js renderer option allows the canvas background to be transparent so the page's CSS background shows through?
options: renderer.transparent = true
scene.background = null
alpha: true in the WebGLRenderer constructor
renderer.setClearColor(0x000000, 0)
questions.explanation: Passing alpha: true to the WebGLRenderer constructor enables a transparent framebuffer. You can also set scene.background = null and clear alpha to 0 after enabling alpha, but the constructor option is the primary switch.

questions.question: In the animation loop you write: model.position.y = Math.sin(t * 0.8) * 0.08. What does multiplying by 0.08 control?
options: The speed of the floating animation
The amplitude - how far the model moves up and down
The number of complete float cycles per second
The easing curve applied to the float
questions.explanation: The 0.08 is the amplitude multiplier - it limits the maximum displacement to 0.08 Three.js units above and below the center. The 0.8 value controls the frequency (how fast it oscillates). Increasing 0.08 makes the float more dramatic.
